storylines.title: Tropical Storm Moke approaches Hawaii
storylines.observation: A tropical system tracking toward the Hawaiian islands tests how a state built for volcanic and wildfire risk handles a wetter, wind-driven threat instead — infrastructure and warning systems calibrated for one hazard profile facing another.
storylines.question: What does a place built to withstand one kind of disaster still owe its residents when a different kind arrives?
storylines.hidden_question: Is preparedness transferable across hazard types, or does every disaster profile require its own dedicated readiness?
storylines.pattern: single-hazard infrastructure meeting a mismatched threat
storylines.why_now: Storm track updates place Hawaii in the warning cone this week, the first significant tropical threat to the islands since recent wildfire recovery efforts began.

history.note: Moke has fully dissipated, its circulation opening into a trough southwest of Hawaii; the Big Island's rain forecast never reached the 15in worst case, and forecasters are calling it a break after Lala's earlier hit.

NWS has a Flood Watch active through Monday afternoon; Big Island rain now running 5-10in with pockets to 15in on saturated ground from Lala. Moke is forecast to weaken to a post-tropical system by midweek.

Moke now sits 310 miles south of Hilo, holding 200-250 miles south of the Big Island through Monday before weakening Wednesday; rain totals revised down, but flood risk persists on ground still saturated from Lala.
Moke's track has firmed up passing about 200 miles south of the Big Island, with weakening forecast to begin Sunday; NOAA now warns over a foot of rain is possible.
Tropical Storm Moke tracking toward Hawaii; National Weather Service Honolulu issuing advisories and watches for the islands.

storylines.title: Canada weighs retaliation in trade dispute with the US
storylines.observation: A long-standing trade relationship between neighbors is being renegotiated through tariffs and countermeasures rather than talks — testing how much economic pain each side will absorb before returning to the table.
storylines.question: When does retaliation become the negotiating strategy rather than a response to one?
storylines.hidden_question: Can two deeply integrated economies actually decouple, or does retaliation just relocate the cost?
storylines.pattern: escalation as bargaining posture between interdependent economies
storylines.why_now: The Trump administration says it will "respond to Canadian retaliation," a day after Carney said Canada had offered to drop its remaining steel, aluminum and auto tariffs if the US lowered its own — an offer Washington's "last-minute changes" scuttled, by Carney's account.

history.note: Carney says Canada had offered to drop its remaining steel/aluminum/auto tariffs if the US lowered its own, blaming Washington's "last-minute changes" for the collapse; the US says it will "respond to Canadian retaliation."

Talks collapsed and 50% US tariffs took effect Saturday on $20B in Canadian goods; Carney announced dollar-for-dollar retaliation on steel, dairy and electronics, effective Sept 8, and called Canada "at war" with the US.
Canada's government signaling new retaliatory measures against US tariffs; talks between Ottawa and Washington remain stalled.

storylines.title: Strait of Hormuz tensions raise new Iranian demands
storylines.observation: A quarter of the world's seaborne oil passes through a chokepoint controlled by a single actor's threats — pricing in a shutdown that has never actually happened but is never fully dismissed either.
storylines.question: How does a market price a threat that is credible but has never been carried out?
storylines.hidden_question: Is the strait's value as leverage greater than its value as a functioning waterway?
storylines.pattern: chokepoint leverage priced as permanent risk premium
storylines.why_now: The Trump administration is expected to announce new economic sanctions on Iran this week, even as Iran and Oman work through their transit-route framework — pressure and workaround advancing on separate, uncoordinated tracks.

history.note: The Trump administration is expected to detail new economic sanctions on Iran this week — Nasdaq already slid Monday partly on the news, even as the Iran-Oman transit talks continue on their own track.

Iran and Oman say they've reached an agreement in principle on a shipping-map framework for transit, still being finalized; the US wants unconditional navigation with no Iranian toll or approval, and Tehran insists it's negotiating only with Muscat, not Washington.
Iran's FM says Tehran is close to an agreement with Oman on a transit route through its own waters — a workaround, not a reopening of the strait itself.
Iran issued new demands tied to Strait of Hormuz shipping this week, pushing oil futures and tanker insurance premiums higher.

storylines.title: Congress keeps voting against the Iran war — and the war keeps going
storylines.observation: The House has twice passed symbolic resolutions to end US involvement in the Iran conflict; the Senate's one attempt at a binding version failed narrowly. Congress keeps registering its objection without ever gaining the power to act on it.
storylines.question: What does losing a vote to end a war actually cost the people who voted to end it?
storylines.hidden_question: Is a non-binding rebuke a real check on executive power, or a way for legislators to be on the record without being responsible for the outcome?
storylines.pattern: symbolic legislative rebuke coexisting with unchanged policy
storylines.why_now: No new congressional action since the July 23 votes; going dormant rather than re-bumping the same stalemate a third time. Worth re-activating if a new resolution is introduced or if casualty trends (18 US troop deaths since February, ~500 injuries) force another vote.

history.note: Correction: Congress has voted on the Iran war three times — House passed non-binding resolutions twice, the Senate's binding version failed 47-49. The standoff isn't a missing vote; it's votes that don't bind.
US naval presence near the strait continues to build without any war powers resolution introduced in Congress.

storylines.title: Flores earthquake recovery continues in Indonesia
storylines.observation: A remote island community rebuilds after a significant earthquake, with recovery paced by geography as much as by the damage itself — aid and materials moving slower than the need for them.
storylines.question: What determines how fast a place is allowed to recover — the disaster, or its distance from the resources to answer it?
storylines.hidden_question: Does remoteness compound disaster damage as much as the disaster itself?
storylines.pattern: remoteness as a second disaster layered on the first
storylines.why_now: BNPB now puts the toll at 100 dead and 1,603 injured, with over 180,000 still displaced — the deadliest earthquake to hit Indonesia since 2022, and the number is still climbing nine days after the quake itself.

history.note: BNPB's toll rose to 100 dead, 1,603 injured, 180,000+ displaced as of Aug 24 — nine days after the quake, still Indonesia's deadliest since 2022, and still not final.
Recovery and rebuilding efforts on Flores continuing this week, with aid logistics slowed by the island's remote terrain.

storylines.title: Gary, Indiana storm outage turns violent
storylines.observation: A severe storm knocked out power to a struggling Rust Belt city, and the extended outage itself became a second, distinct crisis — social order fraying faster than utility crews could restore service.
storylines.question: How long does an outage have to last before it stops being an inconvenience and becomes a breakdown in order?
storylines.hidden_question: Is the storm the disaster, or is the disaster what a fragile city does in the dark?
storylines.pattern: infrastructure failure exposing underlying social fragility
storylines.why_now: NIPSCO reached ~99% restoration across northwest Indiana by 5pm Tuesday, hours ahead of its own deadline, with nearly all of Gary back — but the utility's own caveat still stands: some individual properties with localized damage will take longer than the headline number suggests.

history.note: NIPSCO hit ~99% restoration across NW Indiana by 5pm Tuesday, ahead of its deadline, with nearly all of Gary back on — two weeks after the derecho, and with the utility still cautioning some individual properties will take longer.

Down to ~3,000 customers dark as the Tuesday deadline nears, from 7,000 Monday; NIPSCO itself cautions the deadline won't cover every last property, and Melton says the job isn't done until everyone's back.
A NIPSCO crew vehicle working in Gary was struck by gunfire, pausing restoration before it resumed — happening the same day as NIPSCO's 11:59pm Tuesday restoration deadline.

Braun deployed the National Guard Sunday to help clear routes for crews; Mayor Melton called the pace "unacceptable." About 7,000 Gary customers remained without power Monday morning, down from tens of thousands.
ComEd dispatched 60+ crew members Saturday to join NIPSCO's 600+ linemen restoring Gary; Tuesday's 11:59pm target now carries 95% confidence, per NIPSCO.

storylines.title: Zadar-area arson raises a terrorism question
storylines.observation: A wildfire near a Croatian tourist region is now being investigated as deliberate arson, forcing prosecutors and the public to decide where ordinary criminal fire-setting ends and a terrorism designation begins.
storylines.question: What separates an arsonist from a terrorist when the fire is the same either way?
storylines.hidden_question: Does the terrorism label depend on the act, the intent, or the audience it's meant to frighten?
storylines.pattern: criminal act reclassified under a political threat framework
storylines.why_now: No further reporting has surfaced on the terrorism-charge decision since Turudić's Aug 20 statement; the case is going dormant while prosecutors deliberate rather than being bumped on a stale link.

history.note: Chief state prosecutor Turudić says terrorism isn't excluded but motive is still unestablished; officials now say Zadar's arson arrests and the Omiš fire are separate, unconnected cases.
Croatian prosecutor's office reviewing whether the Omiš-area arson case warrants a terrorism charge rather than standard arson.

storylines.title: mRNA melanoma vaccine advances through regulators
storylines.observation: A personalized cancer vaccine built on mRNA technology developed for COVID-19 is now moving through regulatory review for melanoma — the platform outliving the emergency that funded its development.
storylines.question: What happens to emergency-built technology once the emergency that justified it has passed?
storylines.hidden_question: Was the pandemic the point of mRNA technology, or just its proof of concept?
storylines.pattern: crisis infrastructure outliving its original crisis
storylines.why_now: The same vaccine the FDA rebuffed on an accelerated-approval bid in 2024 has since hit its Phase 3 endpoints and won Breakthrough Therapy status; Moderna's stock surged on the trial result, a reversal of fortune for a program regulators once turned away.

history.note: Context worth naming: the FDA rebuffed Moderna's accelerated-approval bid for this same vaccine in 2024. Phase 3 success and Breakthrough status have since reversed that — Moderna shares jumped sharply on the trial data.
INTerpath-001 trial met both its recurrence and spread-prevention endpoints; the mRNA-4157/Keytruda combo already has FDA Breakthrough Therapy status and a filing is planned within months.
Moderna and Merck's mRNA-4157 personalized melanoma vaccine continued advancing through regulatory review this week.

storylines.title: Markets face Jackson Hole with an unfamiliar Fed chair
storylines.observation: Kevin Warsh's first Jackson Hole keynote as Fed chair arrives with traders still building the dictionary for how his language differs from his predecessor's — the same words may not carry the same signal now that the person saying them has changed.
storylines.question: How long does it take a market to relearn a new voice, and what does it cost while it's still guessing?
storylines.hidden_question: Does monetary credibility belong to the office or the person holding it — and does it transfer automatically, or have to be rebuilt from nothing?
storylines.pattern: institutional continuity undercut by a change in who's speaking
storylines.why_now: Bond and dollar markets are described as "on edge" heading into the symposium (which opens Thursday), with Treasury Secretary Bessent's bond-buyback intervention adding its own pressure on top of what Warsh says Friday around 10am ET — two policy voices now shaping the same trade.

history.note: Bond and dollar markets now described as "on edge" ahead of Thursday's opening, with Bessent's Treasury intervention piling pressure onto Warsh's Friday ~10am ET keynote — two policy actors, one trade.

Nasdaq slid Monday (-0.55%) partly on Iran-sanctions and Canada-tariff news ahead of the symposium; Warsh's Friday speech now shares a data-heavy week with Nvidia earnings, adding more variables traders have to weigh at once.

Symposium dates confirmed Aug 27-29, themed on payments and financial innovation; Warsh has pre-signaled a structural, not near-term-guidance, speech, with consensus expecting neutral language despite 3.4% inflation.
Kevin Warsh, who succeeded Powell as Fed chair in May, delivers his first Jackson Hole keynote Aug 28; markets are still calibrating how to read his language ahead of the September FOMC meeting.

storylines.title: One company's earnings call carries an entire industry's narrative
storylines.observation: Nvidia's quarterly report has become the market's proxy for whether the AI buildout is a durable transformation or an expensive bet — a single earnings call now standing in for a judgment about an entire sector.
storylines.question: What does it mean for a market's confidence to rest this heavily on one company's numbers?
storylines.hidden_question: Is the market pricing an industry, or pricing one company as a stand-in for an industry it has no other way to measure?
storylines.pattern: single company as proxy for an entire industry's narrative
storylines.why_now: Wall Street now has a firm number to clear: $92.2B revenue and $2.09 EPS, +97.4% YoY, reporting after the close Wednesday. Analysts' own base case is that Nvidia beats it anyway and the stock still wobbles — options pricing implies a ~6% swing either way, on gross margin and memory-cost pressure.

history.note: Consensus firmed to $92.2B revenue / $2.09 EPS (+97.4% YoY); analysts' base case is Nvidia beats it and the stock wobbles anyway, with options pricing a ~6% move on gross-margin and memory-cost concerns.
Nvidia reports Q2 FY27 earnings Wednesday, Aug 26, with estimates ranging widely; as the dominant AI-GPU supplier, its guidance is being read as a referendum on the entire AI buildout.

storylines.title: Congo tests whether a peace agreement is real
storylines.observation: Nine months after a US-brokered framework, the first ceasefire verification mission has deployed to eastern Congo — pairing Congolese army and M23 officers with regional and international observers to check whether a signed truce holds up on the ground.
storylines.question: How long does it take a peace agreement to become an actual peace, and who gets to decide when it has?
storylines.hidden_question: Is verification a technical formality, or the point where a peace deal actually gets tested?
storylines.pattern: the gap between a signed agreement and a verified one
storylines.why_now: UN helicopters deployed the first EJVM+ verification mission to Minembwe on Aug 24, pairing three Congolese army officers with three from M23 alongside African Union, Qatari and US observers, days after DRC and M23 emerged from five days of talks in Switzerland with a peace roadmap.

history.note: First EJVM+ ceasefire verification mission deployed to Minembwe, pairing Congolese army and M23 officers with AU/Qatari/US observers, days after DRC and M23 agreed a peace roadmap in Switzerland.

storylines.title: A month where a society changes its behavior for the dead
storylines.observation: Throughout Ghost Month, many Chinese, Taiwanese and diaspora communities avoid travel, major decisions, and celebrations — a lunar calendar month reorganized around the belief that the dead are walking among the living.
storylines.question: What does it cost a society to build a month of restraint around something it can't prove?
storylines.hidden_question: Is the taboo really about the ghosts, or about the discipline of collectively pausing?
storylines.pattern: collective behavior organized around an unverifiable belief
storylines.why_now: Ghost Day, the 15th and most significant day of the lunar Ghost Month, falls Aug 27; in Taiwan especially, many people avoid travel and major life decisions for the entire month, and Hakka communities mark it with large ritual feasts.
storylines.location: China, Taiwan, and Chinese diaspora communities

history.note: Ghost Month is underway, with Ghost Day (the 15th day) falling Aug 27; Taiwan communities especially avoid travel and major decisions for the full month.

storylines.title: A ruling that settles nothing, on purpose
storylines.observation: The Supreme Court paused a lower-court block on Trump's mail-voting order on procedural grounds, while liberal justices explicitly noted the ruling doesn't touch whether the order itself is lawful — leaving the substantive question open ahead of the midterms.
storylines.question: What does it mean for the nation's highest court to rule without ruling on the thing everyone is actually asking?
storylines.hidden_question: Is a procedural stay judicial restraint, or a way of avoiding a decision the court isn't ready to make?
storylines.pattern: a ruling that resolves the process while leaving the substance undecided
storylines.why_now: The Court's stay lets a 23-state-plus-DC challenge proceed on "too early" procedural grounds; Sotomayor and Kagan wrote the decision doesn't address the order's lawfulness, and Jackson dissented sharply, calling the government's stay request "empty, strategic, and bad-faith."

history.note: SCOTUS stayed a lower-court block on Trump's mail-voting order on procedural grounds only; Sotomayor/Kagan noted the lawfulness question remains open, and Jackson dissented, calling the stay bid "bad-faith."

storylines.title: A telescope built to find what we don't have a name for yet
storylines.observation: NASA's Roman Space Telescope, cleared for an Aug 30 liftoff, carries a mirror the size of Hubble's but surveys roughly a hundred times more sky per shot — built for breadth rather than depth, to catch what narrower instruments would miss entirely.
storylines.question: What do you build when the thing you're looking for doesn't have a name yet?
storylines.hidden_question: Is breadth or depth the better strategy for finding something genuinely unexpected?
storylines.pattern: wide-survey instrument built to catch what narrow ones would miss
storylines.why_now: Roman was enclosed in its SpaceX Falcon Heavy fairing Aug 24 ahead of an Aug 30 liftoff from Kennedy Space Center; mission scientists say its wide field could turn up around 100,000 new worlds, more than every prior planet-hunting telescope combined.

history.note: Roman Space Telescope enclosed in its Falcon Heavy fairing Aug 24, on track for an Aug 30 launch; its wide-field design could find ~100,000 new worlds, more than all prior planet-hunting telescopes combined.

storylines.title: Brazil's presidential frontrunners skip their own debate
storylines.observation: Brazil's first televised presidential debate went ahead without either leading candidate — President Lula and Senator Flávio Bolsonaro both stayed away — and one lower-polling candidate then withdrew live, on air, citing Lula's absence as his reason.
storylines.question: What does a debate become when the people most likely to win aren't in it?
storylines.hidden_question: Is skipping the debate a calculated show of strength, or a quiet admission that the format itself has stopped serving frontrunners?
storylines.pattern: leading candidates opting out of the format meant to let voters compare them
storylines.why_now: Band TV's first debate of Brazil's October presidential race went ahead Aug 23 without Lula or Flávio Bolsonaro; Novo's Romeu Zema then pulled out live, on the day, citing Lula's absence, leaving only three lower-polling candidates on stage.

history.note: Brazil's first presidential debate (Aug 23) went ahead without Lula or Flávio Bolsonaro; Novo's Zema then withdrew live, citing Lula's absence, leaving three lower-polling candidates to debate each other.

storylines.title: Armenia jails its most prominent opposition leader the day after declaring for Europe
storylines.observation: Armenian prosecutors detained former president and current opposition-bloc leader Robert Kocharyan on corruption charges one day after PM Pashinyan announced Armenia's EU membership bid — raising the question of whether the case is accountability or a rival cleared from the board at a pivotal moment.
storylines.question: How do you tell an anti-corruption prosecution from a political purge when both can look identical from the outside?
storylines.hidden_question: Does the timing itself become evidence, even when the underlying charges might be entirely legitimate?
storylines.pattern: a legal crackdown landing at the exact moment it most benefits the government's freedom of maneuver
storylines.why_now: Prosecutors detained Kocharyan, 71 — president from 1998-2008 and leader of parliament's second-largest opposition bloc — on abuse-of-authority, bribery and money-laundering charges, a day after Pashinyan set out Armenia's EU membership bid; predecessor Serzh Sargsyan faces charges in the same case, and Kocharyan's bloc calls it a "cynical manifestation of a regime that has lost its legitimacy."
storylines.season_or_time_context: ahead of Armenia's EU accession push

history.note: Kocharyan detained on corruption charges a day after Pashinyan announced Armenia's EU membership bid; predecessor Sargsyan also charged in the same case, and Kocharyan's bloc calls it politically motivated.

storylines.title: Japan and South Korea's leaders get along while their countries drift apart
storylines.observation: A year into PM Takaichi's term, her personal rapport with South Korea's President Lee has held up far better than anyone expected — but analysts warn her rightward domestic agenda and renewed flashpoints are quietly eroding the diplomatic momentum underneath that friendship.
storylines.question: How much does two leaders getting along personally matter when the structures beneath them are pulling apart?
storylines.hidden_question: Is warm top-level diplomacy a genuine bulwark against drift, or just a lagging indicator that hasn't caught up to it yet?
storylines.pattern: personal rapport at the top masking structural drift underneath
storylines.why_now: Marking Takaichi's first year, South Korea's Institute for National Security Strategy warns her conservative agenda, renewed Yasukuni Shrine visits, and the Dokdo/Takeshima dispute risk unwinding the "shuttle diplomacy" gains built on her surprisingly cordial relationship with President Lee Jae-myung.

history.note: A South Korean security institute warns Takaichi's rightward agenda and renewed Yasukuni/Dokdo flashpoints could erode the surprisingly warm Takaichi-Lee rapport that has carried Japan-Korea diplomacy through her first year.
